A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional analyses in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments in an idealized rotation environment, drone tasks, RoboSuite, and modified manipulation environments, with additional empirical analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical comparisons of identity-centered actions and 6D rotation representations.

M1.justification: Sections 2.4.1 and A.3 introduce additive and componentwise-scaled identity biases before quaternion/matrix projection, changing the action-generation procedure. These are localized adaptations; the underlying PPO, SAC, TD3, and recommended local-tangent procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the idealized rotation task, drone tracking and racing, nine RoboSuite tasks, and ReachOrient/PickAndPlaceOrient. The new representation studies reuse these environments; the added RoboSuite average represents existing tasks.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated representation variants. Appendix A.3 compares additive and scaled identity-centered quaternion/matrix actions against existing global and delta variants. Appendix A.4 evaluates Zhou et al.'s 6D representation against matrices across the idealized settings and drone tasks; v1 cited this work without evaluating that representation.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the stated sparse-reward angular tolerance from pi/10 to 0.1 radians. The corresponding original results remain unchanged, so the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the description was corrected. New drone-centering comparisons select the additive variant and explicitly retune hyperparameters using the original sweep settings.

E4.justification: V2 adds systematic ablations testing whether identity centering explains quaternion/matrix performance: uncentered, additive-bias, and scaled-bias variants are compared across algorithms and reward settings in Appendix A.3. Additional drone experiments test centered relative actions against global actions. V1's projection, scaling, exploration, and entropy analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The original run counts and uncertainty displays are retained, including 50-run idealized comparisons, 25-seed drone curves, and five-seed robot benchmarks. The new idealized studies also specify 50 runs. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or formal significance test is documented.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original learning curves retain their values. V2 adds substantial results in Figures 21–31: centering benefits PPO but has mixed effects for SAC/TD3, while 6D-versus-matrix rankings depend on algorithm and action frame. Figure 5 also adds an across-task RoboSuite average. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements between versions under identical settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds mathematical definitions of the two centering maps and range/reachability arguments under bounded network outputs. The existing SO(3) definitions, projection equations, and manifold-entropy argument remain unchanged; no new theorem or substantial proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: action representations influence exploration and optimization, and local-tangent actions provide the most reliable general choice. The added studies support and qualify these retained contributions.

C2.justification: V2 develops an algorithm-dependent interpretation of identity centering and recommends centered relative actions for unstable systems, extending v1's discussion of problematic initialization. It adds cautious explanations of 6D-versus-matrix differences and explicitly excludes discrete-action algorithms. Section 3.3 also softens the description of unscaled SAC failures, although the appendix retains failure examples.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 replaces withholding code pending acceptance with a repository link and a statement that code, training scripts, and reproduction instructions are public; the abstract adds a project link. Appendices A.3–A.4 specify centering formulas and the six-output Gram-Schmidt implementation. Existing code listings and network/tuning details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Schuck et al. (2025b) on differentiable SciPy transformations. It also expands discussion of the already-cited Zhou et al. (2019) and Geist et al. (2024), explaining the relationship between 6D and matrix representations and the choice of matrices for the primary comparison.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are preserved. V2 inserts a centering subsection and hypothesis, adds concise hypothesis summaries, renames Appendix A.2, and inserts two appendix sections before the retained implementation material. Additional changes include localized wording edits, publication headers, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 adds extensive comparison plots in Figures 21–31 and repeats one centering panel as Figure 3. Table 1 gains a delta-action column, the RoboSuite chart gains an average group and revised styling, and noise-distribution figures receive clearer tangent-coordinate axes. Boxed hypothesis summaries also change the main-text presentation; existing figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses two important gaps in v1's comparative evidence: whether initialization contributes to quaternion/matrix disadvantages, and whether the omitted 6D alternative changes the recommendations. The controlled centering ablations and direct 6D comparisons substantially strengthen the practical guidance, including its algorithm-dependent qualifications. Concrete code-access information further improves reproducibility documentation. The unexplained sparse-reward tolerance revision remains a protocol-clarity weakness, particularly because the original results are unchanged.
